provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Surah Al-Balad
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite Surah Al-Balad correctly.
The pupils should be able to explain the meaning of the surah.

Introduction:
We have learned many short surahs in class. Today we will learn Surah Al-Balad which talks about difficult tasks.

Content:
Surah Al-Balad means the city. It refers to Makkah. The surah begins with Allah swearing by this city. The surah mentions the uphill task of freeing a slave and feeding an orphan. It also talks to those who believe and do good deeds.

Class activity:
Pupils will take turns to recite verses from Surah Al-Balad while others listen attentively.

Evaluation questions:
1. What does Surah Al-Balad mean?
2. What does the uphill task refer to?
3. How can we apply the teachings of this surah in our lives?

Summary:
Surah Al-Balad teaches us about difficult tasks and the importance of helping others.

topics.title: Surah Ash-Shams
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite Surah Ash-Shams accurately.
The pupils should be able to explain the main message of purifying the soul.

Introduction:
We have learned about different surahs. Today we will study Surah Ash-Shams which talks about the sun and the soul.

Content:
Surah Ash-Shams means the sun. Allah swears by the sun and its brightness. He also swears by the soul and how He has purified it. The surah mentions that success is for those who purify their souls and failure is for those who corrupt them.

Class activity:
Pupils will write down three ways to keep their souls pure according to Islam.

Evaluation questions:
1. What does Surah Ash-Shams mean?
2. What has Allah purified according to the surah?
3. What happens to those who corrupt their souls?

Summary:
Surah Ash-Shams teaches us that our souls need purification to achieve success.

topics.title: Hadith on knowledge
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the hadith about seeking knowledge.
The pupils should be able to explain the importance of seeking knowledge in Islam.

Introduction:
We have learned about the Quran and surahs. Today we will learn about the importance of seeking knowledge from the hadith.

Content:
The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) said that seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim. He also said that the best of people are those who learn the Quran and teach it. Knowledge helps us understand our religion and live better lives.

Class activity:
Pupils will create a personal study plan for learning Islamic knowledge at home.

Evaluation questions:
1. What did the Prophet say about seeking knowledge?
2. Why is knowledge important in Islam?
3. Name one way you can seek Islamic knowledge daily.

Summary:
Seeking knowledge is a duty in Islam that helps us grow and improve our lives.

topics.title: Fiqh: hajj
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list the main rites of hajj.
The pupils should be able to explain the journey of unity in hajj.

Introduction:
We have learned about the five pillars of Islam. Today we will focus on the pillar of hajj and its importance.

Content:
Hajj is the pilgrimage to Makkah that Muslims perform once in their lifetime if they are able. The main rites include wearing ihram, standing at Arafat, stoning the Jamrat, and sacrificing an animal. These acts show unity among Muslims from all over the world, regardless of wealth or status.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw a simple diagram showing the key locations in hajj and the sequence of rites.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is hajj?
2. Name two main rites of hajj.
3. How does hajj show unity among Muslims?

Summary:
Hajj is a pillar of Islam that demonstrates unity and submission to Allah.

topics.title: Seerah: the farewell sermon
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify the key messages from the farewell sermon.
The pupils should be able to explain the concepts of equality and kindness in Islam.

Introduction:
We have learned about the life of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). Today we will study his last sermon which contains important teachings for all Muslims.

Content:
The farewell sermon was given by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during his last hajj. He emphasized that all humans are equal regardless of race or color. He reminded Muslims to treat their women well and to uphold justice. He also stressed the importance of fulfilling trusts and following the Quran and Sunnah.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in pairs to discuss how they can apply one teaching from the farewell sermon in their daily lives.

Evaluation questions:
1. What did the Prophet say about equality in his farewell sermon?
2. Why is treating women well important in Islam?
3. How can we follow the teachings of the farewell sermon today?

Summary:
The farewell sermon teaches us about equality, justice, and kindness in Islam.

topics.title: Seerah: the legacy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list what Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) left for Muslims.
The pupils should be able to explain how to follow the Prophet's legacy.

Introduction:
We have studied the life of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). Today we will learn about the legacy he left for all Muslims.

Content:
The Prophet left us the Quran as the word of Allah and the Sunnah as his teachings and examples. He also left a community of believers who follow Islam. To follow his legacy, we should follow his way of life, be kind to others, and spread the message of Islam.

Class activity:
Pupils will write a short paragraph about how they can follow one aspect of the Prophet's legacy in their lives.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are two things the Prophet left for Muslims?
2. How can we follow the Prophet's legacy today?
3. Why is it important to follow the Sunnah?

Summary:
The Prophet's legacy includes the Quran and Sunnah which guide us to live good lives.

topics.title: Islamic etiquette
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain the importance of adab in all things.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate excellent manners in different situations.

Introduction:
Islam teaches us how to behave in all aspects of life. Today we will learn about Islamic etiquette or adab.

Content:
Adab means good manners in Islam. It includes how we speak to others, how we eat, how we dress, and how we behave in public. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) taught us to be kind, respectful, and honest in all our actions. Good manners show our faith and bring us closer to Allah.

Class activity:
Pupils will role-play different scenarios showing Islamic etiquette such as greeting elders, eating properly, and speaking politely.

Evaluation questions:
1. What does adab mean?
2. Give an example of Islamic etiquette in daily life.
3. Why are good manners important in Islam?

Summary:
Islamic etiquette teaches us to behave with excellence in all situations to please Allah.

topics.title: Service to humanity
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how Islam encourages charity work.
The pupils should be able to plan a simple service project for their community.

Introduction:
Islam teaches us to care for others and help those in need. Today we will learn about service to humanity in Islam.

Content:
Islam emphasizes charity and helping others. Zakat is one of the five pillars where Muslims give a portion of their wealth to the poor. Sadaqah is voluntary giving. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) said that the best of people are those who benefit others. Service to humanity shows our love for Allah and our fellow humans.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to plan a simple service project to help people in their local community.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is zakat?
2. How does Islam encourage helping others?
3. What service project can you do in your community?

Summary:
Islam teaches us to serve humanity through charity and helping those in need.

topics.title: Preparation for secondary school
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how to maintain their faith in secondary school.
The pupils should be able to list good Islamic habits to keep in secondary school.

Introduction:
As you prepare to move to secondary school, it's important to keep your strong faith. Today we will discuss how to maintain your Islam in the next level of education.

Content:
In secondary school, you will face new challenges. To keep your faith strong, continue praying regularly, make good friends who support your deen, learn more about Islam, and be proud of your religion. Remember that Allah is always with you and will help you stay on the right path.

Class activity:
Pupils will write down three Islamic habits they promise to maintain in secondary school and share with a partner.

Evaluation questions:
1. Why is it important to maintain faith in secondary school?
2. Name two ways to keep your Islam strong in secondary school.
3. How can good friends help you maintain your faith?

Summary:
Keeping good Islamic habits will help you maintain your faith in secondary school.

topics.title: Revision and graduation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall key lessons from the term.
The pupils should be able to write a du'a for their class and future.

Introduction:
Today we will review what we have learned this term and prepare for our graduation with a special prayer.

Content:
We have learned about several surahs, hadith on knowledge, hajj, the seerah of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), Islamic etiquette, service to humanity, and preparing for secondary school. These lessons have taught us how to live as good Muslims. As we graduate, we should make du'a for ourselves, our teachers, and our families.

Class activity:
Pupils will write a collective du'a for their class and future success in secondary school.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is one important thing you learned this term?
2. Why is making du'a important for Muslims?
3. How will you use what you learned in primary 6 in the future?

Summary:
Let's remember our lessons and make du'a for our future as we move to secondary school.
